_comment: Requirements and model inputs for the TURBOFAN version of the IHW3 sizing code. Every number here is a PLACEHOLDER for a generic light twin-turbofan business jet (2 crew + 6 passengers). Replace them with the requirements of YOUR proposed aircraft before you trust any result. Keys that start with an underscore are documentation: jsondecode renames them to x_..., and no code reads them.
_what_changed_from_the_TTPA_file: (1) propulsion is thrust-based: T_SL, a thrust lapse model and TSFC replace P_SL, the piston lapse, BSFC and propeller efficiency. (2) the constraints are FAR 25 (transport category) instead of FAR 23, and every constraint returns a MINIMUM thrust loading T/W instead of a maximum power loading W/P. (3) the aerodynamics adds sweep, compressibility (wave) drag, and a windmilling-engine drag increment in place of the stopped-propeller increment. (4) the weights use the TRANSPORT column of Raymer Table 15.2. (5) the mission segments are jet segments (jet Breguet range and endurance, climb on excess thrust).
_who_reads_what: geometry -> TfGeom. aerodynamics -> TfAero. propulsion -> TfProp. weights -> TfWeights. sizing -> run_tf_sizing -> sizing_mainloop. constraints.conditions -> ConstraintSetImporter.read_conditions -> get_con. constraints.design_point and constraints.W_TO_estimate_lbf -> run_tf_constraints. missions -> MissionProfileReader.read_profile -> get_miss_seg -> run_mission_jet -> mission_fuel.

geometry._comment: SHAPE only. S_ref is written by the sizing loop (or by run_tf_constraints); every span, chord, area and wetted area is a Dependent property of TfGeom recomputed from S_ref on every read.
geometry._src_AR: PLACEHOLDER. Light business jets are typically AR 7-9 (Raymer Table 4.1 gives about 7.5 for jet transports/business jets).
geometry._src_taper_ratio: PLACEHOLDER. Raymer Fig. 4.24: a quarter-chord sweep of about 25 deg wants a taper ratio near 0.3-0.4.
geometry._src_sweep_quarter_chord_deg: PLACEHOLDER. Used now: it sets the leading-edge sweep (which picks the Oswald-efficiency formula) and the drag-divergence Mach number (Korn equation).
geometry._src_thickness_ratio: PLACEHOLDER supercritical sections. The MEAN goes into the wetted area (Raymer Eq. 7.12) and into the Korn drag-divergence equation; the ROOT goes into the Torenbeek fuel-volume equation.
geometry._src_twist_incidence_dihedral: Reporting only - not read by the sizing loop.

horizontal_tail._src: Raymer Table 6.4, jet transport: c_HT = 1.00. Arm and planform are PLACEHOLDERS - measure them off your layout. S_ht = c_HT * S_ref * MAC / arm [Raymer Eq. 6.29]. For a T-tail Raymer allows about 5 % less.

vertical_tail._src: Raymer Table 6.4, jet transport: c_VT = 0.09. Arm and planform are PLACEHOLDERS. S_vt = c_VT * S_ref * b / arm [Raymer Eq. 6.28]. Note: a twin with wing-mounted engines may need MORE vertical tail for engine-out control - check it.

fuselage._comment: Cabin-driven, so CONSTANT through the sizing loop. PLACEHOLDER layout: 6 passenger seats in a 2-abreast club arrangement plus a 2-seat cockpit.
fuselage._src_lengths: PLACEHOLDER. Total 42 ft, a fineness ratio of about 6.7.

nacelle._comment: One nacelle per engine. Unlike the piston TTPA, BOTH the length AND the diameter follow the engine, because a turbofan's diameter grows with thrust (Raymer Eq. 10.3). The two factors below stretch the BARE engine into its nacelle (inlet lip, cowl, exhaust).
nacelle._src: Layout assumptions, NOT textbook values. Measure them off your layout when you have one.

landing_gear._src: Raymer Ch. 11 static-load ratios; PLACEHOLDERS until a weight-and-balance study fixes the cg envelope. Used only by landing_gear_loads, after the loop.

aerodynamics._comment: Clean CD0 is computed from the geometry (Raymer Eq. 12.23, CD0 = Cfe * S_wet/S_ref). Compressibility (wave) drag is added on top of it at the flight Mach number by the Korn equation plus Lock's fourth-power law. The configuration polars add flap, gear and windmilling-engine increments.
aerodynamics._src_Cfe: Raymer Table 12.3: civil transport 0.0026, bomber/transport 0.0030 range; 0.0030 is a reasonable business-jet value. PLACEHOLDER.
aerodynamics._src_CD0_reference: CHECK VALUE only (nothing computes with it): a typical clean business-jet CD0, printed next to the computed one.
aerodynamics._src_airfoil_type: PLACEHOLDER supercritical section, typical of business jets. Options: 'supercritical' (Korn kappa_A 0.95: flat-topped, aft-loaded section) or 'conventional' (0.87: NACA 6-series style). 'custom' uses korn_technology_factor instead. The type only moves the Korn drag-divergence Mach in this model; handling effects are not modelled. Override per run with run_tf_constraints/run_tf_sizing(..., 'airfoil', 'conventional') or trade it with airfoil_sweep_study.
aerodynamics._src_CLmax_reference_sweep_deg: The quarter-chord sweep the three CLmax values above are quoted at. TfAero scales all three by cos(sweep)/cos(this) when geometry.sweep_quarter_chord_deg differs (Raymer Sec. 12.4), so a sweep change also costs CLmax. Remove the key to use CLmax as given at any sweep.
aerodynamics._src_CLmax: Roskam Part I Table 3.1, business jets: clean 1.4-1.8, takeoff 1.6-2.2, landing 1.6-2.6. PLACEHOLDERS - mid-range.
aerodynamics._src_increments: Roskam Part I Table 3.6 (same table the TTPA used): takeoff flaps 0.010-0.020, landing flaps 0.055-0.075, gear 0.015-0.025; e drops about 0.05 (takeoff flaps) and 0.10 (landing flaps).
aerodynamics._src_delta_CD0_windmilling_engine: Drag of the failed engine (windmilling fan plus spillage), added in the one-engine-inoperative conditions. Replaces the stopped-propeller increment of the TTPA. PLACEHOLDER: Torenbeek Appendix G gives methods; 0.002-0.005 is typical for a small turbofan.

propulsion._comment: Thrust-based. T_SL is the SEA-LEVEL STATIC, INSTALLED, TAKEOFF-RATED thrust of ALL engines [lbf]; the sizing loop writes it as W_TO * (T/W). The thrust lapse and the TSFC models are generic high-bypass turbofan models; replace them with your candidate engine's deck when you have one.
propulsion._src_bypass_ratio: PLACEHOLDER. Small business-jet turbofans are BPR 3-5. Enters the engine weight and diameter regressions (Raymer Eqs. 10.1 and 10.3).
propulsion._lapse_and_tsfc_options: Two engine types. HIGH bypass (BPR ~4+): lapse_model and tsfc_model = 'mattingly_hbtf'. LOW bypass, dry, subsonic (BPR below ~1.5, no afterburner): lapse_model and tsfc_model = 'mattingly_lbtf'. Set BOTH keys to the same type and set bypass_ratio to match (the engine weight and diameter regressions read it). For a low-bypass engine Mattingly suggests a throttle ratio near 1.0-1.08. tsfc_model can also be 'constant' (uses tsfc_constant_per_hr).
propulsion._src_lapse_model: 'mattingly_hbtf' is Mattingly, Heiser and Pratt, Aircraft Engine Design, 2nd ed., Eq. (2.54a), high-bypass turbofan, maximum power: alpha = delta_0 * (1 - 0.49*sqrt(M0)) when theta_0 <= TR, and delta_0 * (1 - 0.49*sqrt(M0) - 3*(theta_0 - TR)/(1.5 + M0)) when theta_0 > TR. Check the equation against your edition. 'mattingly_lbtf' is Mattingly AED 2nd ed. Eq. (2.54b), low-bypass mixed-flow turbofan at military (maximum DRY) power, divided by its 0.6 so that alpha = 1 at sea-level static and T_SL is the DRY static thrust: alpha = delta_0 when theta_0 <= TR, delta_0 * (1 - 3.8*(theta_0 - TR)/theta_0) when theta_0 > TR.
propulsion._src_throttle_ratio: TR = theta_0 at which the engine reaches its turbine-temperature limit (Mattingly Sec. 2.3). 1.0-1.1 is typical for a civil turbofan. PLACEHOLDER.
propulsion._src_tsfc_model: 'mattingly_hbtf' is Mattingly AED 2nd ed. Eq. (3.55a), high-bypass turbofan: TSFC = (0.45 + 0.54*M0) * sqrt(theta) [1/hr]. 'mattingly_lbtf' is Mattingly AED 2nd ed. Eq. (3.55b), low-bypass mixed-flow turbofan at military (dry) power: TSFC = (0.9 + 0.30*M0) * sqrt(theta) [1/hr]. 'constant' uses tsfc_constant_per_hr everywhere.
propulsion._src_T_TO_over_T_max_continuous: Takeoff thrust / maximum continuous thrust. PLACEHOLDER; about 1.05-1.15 for a civil turbofan. Used by the conditions that set max_continuous = true and by the climb segments.
propulsion._src_installation_loss_fraction: Inlet, bleed and power-extraction losses. The constraint analysis works with INSTALLED thrust; the driver divides by (1 - this) to report the UNINSTALLED thrust you would compare against an engine catalogue. PLACEHOLDER: 3-8 % is typical.
propulsion._src_design_mach: Maximum operating Mach number, which enters the engine LENGTH regression (Raymer Eq. 10.2).
propulsion._src_engine_regression: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, Eqs. 10.1-10.3, 'rubber engine' statistical model for a NON-afterburning turbojet/turbofan, PER ENGINE, T in lbf (takeoff thrust of one engine): W = 0.084 T^1.1 exp(-0.045 BPR) [lb], L = 0.185 T^0.4 M^0.2 [ft], D = 0.033 T^0.5 exp(0.04 BPR) [ft]. Check the coefficients against your edition.
propulsion._src_thrust_range_of_validity_lbf: Range over which TfProp does not warn. Generous: the Raymer fit is a broad statistical trend.

weights._comment: Raymer Table 15.2 component build-up. Raymer prints three columns - fighter, transport/bomber and general aviation - and NONE fits a light business jet: the transport column (wing 10, tails 5.5, fuselage 5.0 psf, all-else 0.17 W0) is calibrated on airliners and gives this 16,000 lb airplane an empty-weight fraction of about 0.70, which does not close; the GA column is calibrated on unpressurised piston airplanes and is too light. The unit weights below are PLACEHOLDERS set between the two columns. CALIBRATE THEM before trusting the result: the usual way is to run the build-up on one or two existing business jets of the same size (known S_ref, OEW, thrust) and scale the unit weights until the build-up reproduces their OEW. The statistical cross-check printed by run_tf_sizing is a first sanity check.
weights._src_W_payload: PLACEHOLDER: 2 crew + 6 passengers at 200 lb each (1600 lb) plus 400 lb of baggage.
weights._src_unit_weights: PLACEHOLDERS between Raymer Table 15.2 GA (wing 2.5, tails 2.0, fuselage 1.4 psf) and transport (10, 5.5, 5.0 psf). Wing and tails multiply planform area (EXPOSED for the wing; the tails use their full volume-coefficient area, slightly conservative); the fuselage multiplies WETTED area.
weights._src_fractions: Raymer Table 15.2: landing gear 0.043 W0 and installed engine 1.3 x bare (transport column). All-else-empty 0.15 W0 is a PLACEHOLDER between GA (0.10) and transport (0.17).
weights._src_statistical_empty: Raymer Table 3.1, jet transport: We/W0 = 1.02 * W0^-0.06. CROSS-CHECK ONLY (OEW_statistical); the loop uses the build-up. Business jets often sit a few percent above this line.
weights._src_fuel_density: Jet-A at 15 degC, about 6.7 lb/US gal = 50.1 lb/ft^3. Used only by the post-sizing wing fuel-volume check.

sizing._comment: Read by run_tf_sizing and handed to sizing_mainloop. Three states are iterated: W_0, T_SL and S_ref.
sizing._src_relaxation: Under-relaxation factor, x <- x + w (x_new - x). Changes the PATH, not the answer. run_tf_sizing retries with smaller values if this one does not close.

constraints._comment: FAR 25 constraint conditions. Every condition returns the MINIMUM installed sea-level-static takeoff thrust loading (T/W)_TO it allows, except landing, which returns the MAXIMUM wing loading (a vertical wall).
constraints._condition_keys: type: takeoff | landing | climb_gradient | flight. Optional keys and their defaults (see get_con): config 'clean', beta 1.0 (W_condition/W_TO), throttle 1.0, oei false, max_continuous false, engine_out_drag false, mach 0, n 1, Ps_fps 0, speed_over_stall 1.2.
constraints._src_W_TO_estimate_lbf: Used ONLY by run_tf_constraints, the diagram-only driver, to turn the chosen (T/W) into a thrust: T_SL = (T/W) * W_TO. run_tf_sizing replaces it with the converged weight.

design_point._src: PLACEHOLDER design point. Pick yours off the diagram, backed away from the least-thrust corner for margin.

conditions.name: Takeoff FAR 25
conditions._src: FAR 25 takeoff field length (balanced field, includes the engine failure) of 4,500 ft at sea level, standard day. PLACEHOLDER. Roskam Part I Sec. 3.4: s_TOFL = 37.5 * TOP25, TOP25 = (W/S)_TO / (sigma * CLmax_TO * (T/W)_TO).

conditions.name: Landing FAR 25
conditions._src: FAR 25 landing field length of 3,600 ft at sea level. PLACEHOLDER. Roskam Part I Sec. 3.4: s_FL = 0.3 * V_A^2 (V_A in kt), V_A = 1.3 V_sL. beta = 0.85 is a typical maximum landing weight / takeoff weight for a business jet.

conditions.name: 1st segment OEI
conditions._src: FAR 25.121(a), twin: positive gradient (> 0) with the gear down, takeoff flaps, one engine inoperative, at V_LOF (taken as 1.2 V_s).

conditions.name: 2nd segment OEI
conditions._src: FAR 25.121(b), twin: 2.4 % gradient, gear up, takeoff flaps, one engine inoperative, at V2 = 1.2 V_s. Usually the climb requirement that sizes a twin.

conditions.name: En-route OEI
conditions._src: FAR 25.121(c), twin: 1.2 % gradient, clean, one engine inoperative at maximum continuous thrust, at 1.25 V_s.

conditions.name: Approach climb OEI
conditions._src: FAR 25.121(d), twin: 2.1 % gradient with approach flaps (taken here as takeoff flaps), gear up, one engine inoperative, at landing weight, at no more than 1.5 V_s (Roskam Part I Sec. 3.4).

conditions.name: Balked landing AEO
conditions._src: FAR 25.119: 3.2 % gradient, landing flaps, gear down, all engines operating, at landing weight, at 1.3 V_s.

conditions.name: Cruise
conditions._src: Cruise at M 0.75, 41,000 ft, at maximum continuous thrust, at a mid-cruise weight of 0.92 W_TO. PLACEHOLDER. Mattingly master equation with n = 1 and Ps = 0: thrust equals drag.

conditions.name: Initial cruise ceiling
conditions._src: Able to climb at 300 ft/min (Ps = 5 ft/s) at the start of cruise, 41,000 ft and M 0.72, at MAXIMUM CLIMB thrust (modelled as the full rating, max_continuous = false). PLACEHOLDER - this is the usual way an 'initial cruise altitude capability' requirement is written.

std_mission._description: Business-jet design mission: start/taxi/takeoff, climb, cruise, descent, climb, loiter (hold), descent, landing. PLACEHOLDER numbers.
std_mission._src_reserve: Reserve and trapped-fuel allowance applied on top of the mission fuel. PLACEHOLDER - NBAA-style IFR reserves are often written as a separate alternate + hold; the hold is modelled as the loiter segment here.
std_mission._src_climb_schedule: Climb segments fly a constant EQUIVALENT airspeed (keas) until the true airspeed reaches the Mach number given by 'mach', then hold that Mach - the usual jet climb schedule (e.g. 250 KEAS / M 0.70). The crossover altitude is where the two meet.
std_mission._src_fixed_fractions: Roskam Part I Table 2.1, business jets: start 0.990 x taxi 0.995 x takeoff 0.995 = 0.980; descent 0.990; landing/taxi/shutdown 0.992. Unlike the TTPA code, these are READ from each segment's weight_fraction key, not hardcoded.
